proposals.observation: In the last 48 hours, 11 sessions hit the quiz. Nine of them stalled at intro_load and never reached q1_shown. Only 1 reached the email gate. Zero completions. The bottleneck is not the quiz questions — it is whatever happens between the page rendering and the first question appearing. Nine people looked at the intro screen and left.
proposals.proposal: The intro screen is losing 82% of sessions before a single question loads. The most likely culprits are a slow asset load, a wall of explanatory text, or a call-to-action button that does not feel worth pressing. Audit QuizIntro.astro for three things: (1) any image or script blocking the first interactive paint, (2) copy length — if the intro text runs beyond 60 words it needs cutting, and (3) the button label. Current button labels like "Start Quiz" or "Find Out Now" pass the Sultanic test only if they carry something specific to Joel's framing. Replace vague button text with a line that names the actual thing the person is about to discover. A line like "See which money pattern is running your decisions" is grounded in the quiz's behavioural premise and costs nothing to ship.
proposals.new_text: See which money pattern is running your decisions

proposals.impact: lift Money Worship open rate toward 66% benchmark
proposals.observation: Money Vigilance has a 66.67% open rate across 12 sends. Money Worship sits at 37.5% across 16 sends — the largest open-rate gap in the automation set, 29 percentage points below the top performer. The subject line is the most testable single variable between those two automations, and it is the one change that fits in a single file edit.
proposals.proposal: Pull the subject line approach from the Money Vigilance sequence and apply the same structural logic to Money Worship's first email. Vigilance likely opens because its subject names a recognisable internal experience rather than a label or a promise. Money Worship subscribers have told the quiz they over-invest meaning in money — they are not looking for a badge, they are looking for someone who has noticed something true about them. The current subject line almost certainly names the pattern ("You're a Money Worshipper") rather than the feeling beneath it. Rewrite the subject to name the feeling: the creeping sense that earning more should have settled something by now, but hasn't.
proposals.current_text: subject: You're a Money Worshipper — here's what that means
proposals.new_text: subject: You earn more than you used to. It still doesn't feel like enough.

proposals.observation: Two CI workflows failed in the last 24 hours: "Daily Blog Post" at 07:54 and "Funnel-Hack Digest" at 12:58. The content queue shows only 1 post queued and 47 published. With the Daily Blog Post workflow broken, that queued post will not publish on schedule and the pipeline that feeds organic traffic stops. This is the highest-urgency fix because every day the workflow stays broken is a day without a published post and without the SEO surface area that drives quiz entries.
proposals.proposal: Open the Daily Blog Post workflow file and check the run log for the 07:54 failure. The most common causes in Astro-based content pipelines are: a missing or rotated API key in GitHub Secrets, a changed content schema that the build step can no longer parse, or a Node version mismatch after a dependency update. The recent commit "chore(state): update quiz-last-seen cursor" touched state files — if that commit altered anything in src/content.config.ts indirectly (via a shared import), the build will reject it. Confirm the error message in the Actions log, then fix the specific broken line. Do not touch .github/workflows/daily-blog-post.yml itself (it is a blocked path) — the fix will be in whichever source file the log names as the parse or build error.
